one_line_summary: Japanese patent for an omnidirectional moving vehicle with two (or more) active casters, each having a motor-driven 360 degree steering shaft and an offset drive wheel whose drive actuator is body-mounted and geared through the steering axis, the two casters being mirror-symmetric so drive-reaction disturbance torques on the steering shafts cancel.

E1.quote: The omnidirectional moving vehicle 1 is provided with four casters with respect to the vehicle body 2, and these four casters enable the vehicle body 2 to move freely with respect to the floor surface 3.
E1.note: Four-caster wheeled vehicle base, but a generic omnidirectional moving vehicle; no cart, trolley, bed, heavy-load or delicate-transport application is mentioned.

E2.quote: Of the four casters, two are active casters 5 having drive wheels 4 to which rotational torque is transmitted, and the remaining two are driven casters 6 that are pulled from the vehicle body 2 to rotate.
E2.note: Exactly two of four casters are active, each with its own steering actuator 8 (360 degree rotation of support member 51) and drive actuator 9: steer-and-drive modules. Claim 1 also covers 'a plurality'; a variant with three or more active casters is mentioned.

E3.quote: The two active casters 5 are provided closer to the front side of the vehicle body 2 (to the left of the paper in FIG. 2), and the two driven casters 6 are behind the vehicle body 2
E3.note: The other two wheels are passive free-swivel (driven) casters 6, as in the idea, but the two active casters are both at the front side, coaxial when aligned forward (and claim 2 places them so drive axes coincide), i.e. side by side, not diagonal.

E4.note: No handlebar, joystick or handle sensors described; the user interface is not addressed.

E5.note: No user force sensing and no conversion of handle force into a motion vector; speed/acceleration mentioned only as wheel acceleration causing disturbance torque.

E6.quote: the vehicle body 2 is arbitrarily controlled by coordinating the steering actuator 8 and the driving actuator 9 of the first active caster 5A and the second active caster 5B.
E6.note: Coordinated control of each active caster's steering actuator and drive actuator to move the body in an arbitrary direction at any speed, i.e. per-wheel steering angle plus drive from a desired motion. But no derivation from a handle-force vector, and the control law is not detailed (also covers rotation, three DOF).

combination_note: Discloses E2 (two 360 degree steer-and-drive active casters plus two passive free-swivel casters on a four-caster base) and, generically, E6 (coordinated steering angle and drive per active caster for arbitrary-direction motion). It does not place the active casters diagonally (they are side by side at the front, coaxial), so E2+E3 is only partially met. It has nothing on E4/E5: no push handle, no force sensing, no force-to-translation-vector conversion using speed/acceleration. Closest gap to the idea: diagonal placement and the handle-force-driven power-assist control chain E4->E5->E6.

limitations.limitation: An omnidirectional moving vehicle in which a plurality of active casters are mounted on the vehicle body and the vehicle body can be moved in all directions on the floor surface
limitations.quote: a plurality of active casters are mounted on the vehicle body and the vehicle body can be moved in all directions on the floor surface
limitations.reason: Idea has two steer-and-drive (active caster-type) modules plus free-swivel casters, so the platform can translate in any direction.

limitations.limitation: The active caster has a steering shaft arranged along the vertical direction
limitations.quote: The active caster is Steering shafts arranged along the vertical direction,
limitations.reason: A 360 degree steering drive necessarily rotates the wheel about a vertical steering axis.

limitations.limitation: A mounting portion fixed to the vehicle body that rotatably holds the steering shaft
limitations.quote: A mounting portion that is fixed to the vehicle body and rotatably holds the steering shaft,
limitations.reason: Any steer module bolted to the cart frame has a housing that rotatably holds its steering axis.

limitations.limitation: A support member fixed to the steering shaft that is given a steering angle according to the rotation of the steering shaft
limitations.quote: A support member that is fixed to the steering shaft and is given a steering angle according to the rotation of the steering shaft.
limitations.reason: The wheel fork/yoke of a steer-and-drive wheel turns with the steering axis to set the steering angle.

limitations.limitation: A drive wheel with a horizontal axle held by the support member at a position offset horizontally by a predetermined distance from the steering shaft rotation center (caster offset)
limitations.reason: Idea does not specify a caster trail/offset; many swerve modules have the contact point on the steering axis (zero offset).

limitations.limitation: A steering actuator fixed to the mounting portion that rotationally drives the steering shaft
limitations.reason: Idea has a steering drive, but whether it is fixed to the body-side mounting portion is unspecified.

limitations.limitation: A drive actuator fixed to the mounting portion (not to the rotating support member) that rotationally drives the drive wheel
limitations.reason: Idea does not specify motor location; a hub motor on the rotating fork would not meet this.

limitations.limitation: A transmission means including at least one rotation transmitting member rotatably held relative to the steering shaft, converting vertical-axis rotation into horizontal-axis rotation and transmitting torque from the drive actuator to the drive wheel
limitations.reason: Idea does not specify the drive train (coaxial gear/bevel transmission versus in-wheel motor).

limitations.limitation: The plurality of active casters include a first and a second active caster having structures mirror-symmetrical to each other with respect to the vertical axis
limitations.reason: Idea does not specify mirror-symmetric module construction; possible but not stated.
